First Solar indicates that Series 7 modules produced in the dc dc United States have 100% domestic sources for components listed in the U.S. Treasury domestic content guidance, providing significant added value over other available modules in the marketplace (including its own imported modules). While its Vietnamese and Malaysian facilities remain active, imports of CdTe modules from those countries into the United States fell in 2024 by an estimated 15%. Some of this decline was replaced by shipments from India into the United States, but due to a suspected mislabeling issue, this is difficult to corroborate in public data. In general, balance-of-module components are imported for Series 6 modules—from trade partners such as Malaysia—while components for Series 7 modules produced in the United States come from domestic suppliers. There is enough domestic production of cadmium for 6 GW of modules. No tellurium or selenium refining exists in the United States. First Solar dc partners with 5N Plus in Canada to refine U.S. tellurium and produce CdTe powder. Some of the tellurium-containing residues 5N Plus refines come from Utah, but the company also sources tellurium elsewhere. Given that Canada’s leading source of imported tellurium is China, the world’s leading producer (which in early 2025 placed export control on tellurium and CdTe compounds), there is a high probability that the CdTe modules produced in the United States in 2024 relied on tellurium from China. Structural Products The United States hosts a growing base of manufacturing capacity for many PV system structural components, particularly for utility-scale systems. Some elements—such as torque tubes, piles, and select tracker assemblies—are widely produced domestically due to their size and shipping constraints. Others, such as fasteners and certain rooftop components, still rely heavily on imports. Major steel components used in utility-scale PV systems represent only a small fraction of total steel consumption in the United States, which overall relies mostly (87%) on domestic steel mills for its products. China is a major steel producer as well as a dominant manufacturer of finished PV steel products. Given China’s scale, low labor costs, and political strategy to export cheap goods, its products are often sold at a significant discount in global markets. As a result, both raw and finished steel products from China are a part of some U.S. PV installations. However, the United States maintains its presence in steel’s upstream supply chain through domestic iron ore production.
